name: Zardozi Metallic Embroidery
history: An opulent Persian-origin court embroidery using real gold (Zar) and silver threads, beads, sequins, and metallic wires.
care: Dry clean only. Store wrapped in soft muslin cloth.

name: Ajrakh Mud-Resist Block Print
history: A 16-stage resist dyeing tradition using hand-carved wooden blocks and 100% botanical dyes like Indigo, Madder, and Tamarind paste.
care: Gentle hand wash in cold water with mild eco-detergent.

name: Lucknowi Chikankari
history: A 400-year-old delicate white-on-white and pastel needlecraft involving 32 distinct stitches including Bakhiya (shadow work) and Murri (rice knot).
care: Hand wash or gentle dry clean. Iron on reverse.

name: Pochampally Double Ikat
history: An intricate geometric weaving technique where both warp and weft yarns are tie-dyed with pinpoint precision before being loaded on the handloom.
care: Hand wash in cold water; dry in shade to preserve loom vibrancy.

name: Shantiniketan Kantha Stitch
history: A folk narrative embroidery technique utilizing variations of running stitches to create organic depictions of folklore, birds, and floral vines.
care: Gentle dry clean or soft hand wash.

name: Bagru Dabu Mud-Resist
history: An ancient technique involving applying a clay, gum, and sawdust paste onto cloth before dipping into subterranean indigo and kashish dye pits.
care: Wash separately for the first two washes in cold water.
